rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trial is God's test; misguidance and guidance disclose in the witnessed world what was already known in the unseen.
rows.anchor: أي الفتنة التي أوقعها السفهاء { إلا فتنتك } أي ابتلاؤك واختياك { تضل بها من تشاء } أي تظهر في عالم الشهادة من ضلاله ما كان معلوما لك في عالم الغيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses acknowledges God alone as guardian and source of their welfare; God gains or loses nothing, while pardon benefits them and vengeance harms them, and divine acts are not driven by purposes.
rows.anchor: لا يقدر على عمل مصالحنا غيرك , وأنت لا نفع لك في شيء من الأمرين ولا ضر , بل الكل بالنسبة إليك على حد سواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because a guardian brings benefit and removes harm, asking forgiveness means erasing sins and asking mercy means raising them.
rows.anchor: فاغفر لنا } أي امح ذنوبنا { وارحمنا } أي ارفعنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask for a good, contented and wholesome life in this present, lowly world and a similar good in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: في هذه الدنيا } أي الحاضرة والدنية { حسنة } أي عيشة راضية طيبة { وفي } الحياة { الآخرة } أي كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their repentance explains the request; beginning with God's lordship and then their servanthood gives two powerful causes of happiness and teaches repentance, submission, and avoidance of their former error.
rows.anchor: فبدأ بذكر عزة الربوبية وثنى بذلة العبودية وهما أقوى اسباب السعادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the sin was publicly asking to see God, the wording of repentance alludes to returning to truth, becoming sound and gentle, and restraining speech; the name Judah is linked to this as an exhortation to repent.
rows.anchor: تنبيها لهم على أن اسمهم يدل على التوبة والرجوع إلى الحق والصيرورة إلى الصلاح واللين والضعف في الصوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' apparent objection to destroying the obedient for the sinners is coaxing and entreaty; he knows God's act is just and that God may do as He wills.
rows.anchor: على سبيل الاستعطاف منه والتملق مع العلم بأنه عدل منه تعالى وله أن يفعل ما يشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God says His punishment may strike whomever He wills, whether that person sinned or did not sin.
rows.anchor: أصيب به } أي في الدنيا والآخرة { من أشاء } أي اذنب أو لم يذنب

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A report in the Ṣaḥīḥ says God's mercy preceded His anger, with a variant reading that it overcame His anger; the author allows either sense.
rows.anchor: حديث أبي هريرة في الصحيح ( إن رحمتي سبقت ) وفي رواية : غلبت - ( غضبي )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mercy has wider scope than wrath: everything subject to wrath also receives mercy through creation and provision, whereas many creatures receive mercy without wrath, including animals, inanimate things, believers, angels, and houris.
rows.anchor: كل ما تعلق به الغضب تعلقت به الرحمة بإيجاد وإضافة الرزق عليه , ولا عكس كالحيونات العجم والجمادات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although mercy encompasses everything, God promises its enduring share to the God-conscious, so the breadth of mercy does not oblige Him to give its continuance to everyone.
rows.anchor: فسأكتبها } اي اخص بدوامها بوعد لا خلف فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Piety means avoiding what God forbids and doing what He commands; zakat is singled out because it was due at this appointed meeting and is a trust between people and God, like following the Prophet's described traits.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكر نظرهم إلى الخالق بالانتهاء عما عنه والاتئمار بما أمر به , أتبعه النظر إلى الخلائق فقال : { ويؤتون الزكاة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final condition generalizes the fruit of piety: believers affirm all God's signs in heart and speech and confirm that faith by action, without accepting some signs and rejecting others.
rows.anchor: والذين هم بآباتنا } اي كلها { يؤمنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountain was like a roof directly above the Israelites; their belief that it was falling is literal, and the wording 'upon them' conveys its swift closeness.
rows.anchor: كأنه ظلة } أي سقف , وحقق أنه صار عليهم موازيا لهم من جهة الفوق كالسقف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Israelites are said to have prostrated on their left brows and watched the mountain with the right eye in fear; they still perform this prostration and call it the one that lifted punishment.
rows.anchor: خر كل منهم ساجدا على حاجبه الأيسر , وصار ينظر بعينه اليمنى إلى الجبل فزعا من سقوطه , وهي سنة في سجودهم إلى الآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking the covenant with strength means firm resolve to bear its demands; remembering what the Torah contains means not forgetting any commands or prohibitions, so they may become God-conscious.
rows.anchor: خذوا ما آتيناكم } أي بعظمتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The covenant reinforces all the book's obligations, including speaking only truthfully about God and concealing none of it.
rows.anchor: تأكيد المواثيق عليهم في أخذ جميع مافي الكتاب الذي من جملته ألا تقولوا على الله إلا الحق ولا تكتموا شيئا منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says that when Moses recited the tablets, every tree, mountain, and stone on earth shook; Jews still shake their heads when hearing the Torah.
rows.anchor: ولما قرأة موسى عليه السلام الأولواح وفيها كتاب الله لم يبق على الأرض شجر ولا جبل ولا حجر إلا اهتز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The covenant theme expands to all humanity: reason and clear signs make God's unity evident, yet in mercy God delayed accountability until sending messengers with books and further explanations; greater knowledge brings greater blame.
rows.anchor: في عموم هذا النوع الآدمي من العقول ونصب من الأدلة الوضحة للأمر إيضاح المشهود للشاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording emphasizes strong covenants: descendants are taken from the stronger human kind, males, and from the strongest bodily part, each father's back; their constitution gives capacity to obey, so the command is within ability.
rows.anchor: ذكر أخذ الذرية من أقوى نوعي الآدمي , وهمالذكور فقال : { من بني آدم } وذكر أنه من أمتن الأعضاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's making people witnesses means presenting proofs through their intellect, the heavens and earth, and messengers supported by miracles, which testify that He alone is Lord.
rows.anchor: ومن إرسال الرسل المؤيدين بالمعجزات ما كانوا كالشهود بأنه لا رب غيره

rows.speaker: الإمام حجة الإسلام الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazālī explains the verse as the souls' assent rather than a spoken response: souls are naturally disposed to recognize realities and, on recognizing God's oneness, lordship, and mercy, are moved by fear and hope to obey.
rows.anchor: الإمام حجة الإسلام الغزالي في الكلام على العقل من باب العلم من الإحياء فإنه قال معنى هذه الآية : والمراد إقرار نفوسهم , لا إقرار الألسنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer 'yes, we bear witness' is witnessed knowledge: after the proofs they reached a point where no other answer was possible, as though they had uttered it.
rows.anchor: قالوا بلى شهدنا } أي كان علما شهوديا , وذلك لأنهم وصلوا بعد البيان إلى حد لا يكون فيه الجواب إلا ذلك فكأنهم قالوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses about all creatures submitting to God (13:15 and 16:49) illustrate the prior testimony: the scene is representation, making the ability to infer like actual witnessing.
rows.anchor: ولله يسجد من في السموات والأرض طوعا وكرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose of this testimony is to prevent people pleading at Judgment that they lacked evidence of God's unity or merely followed their idolatrous ancestors without a messenger to alert them.
rows.anchor: فعلة كراهة { أن يقولوا يوم القيامة } أي إن لم ينصب لهم الأدلة { إنا كنا هن هذا }

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says that without covenant or messenger the disbelievers would claim either ignorance or blind following of their ancestors, and ask why they should be punished for their forebears' misguidance.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حيان : والمعنى أن الكفرة لو لم يؤخذ عليهم عهد ولا جاءهم رسول بما تضمنه العهد

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas's report in the Ṣaḥīḥ says that the least-punished person in Hell would ransom himself with all earthly possessions, but God had asked him in Adam's loins for the easier act of avoiding association and he refused.
rows.anchor: حديث أنس في الصحيح ( يقول الله لأهون أهل النار عذابا : لو أن لك ما في الأرض من شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author takes the covenant in Adam's loins as the installation of evidence and presentation of truth in a form enabling sound reasoning, which explains why mention of ancestral imitation conflicts with a literal spoken pledge.
rows.anchor: والأخذ وهو في الصلب إنما هو بنصب الأدلة وتقرير الحق على و جه مهيئ للاستدلال بتركيب العقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This interpretation does not contradict reports of an actual address in the realm of atoms, if those reports are sound; the author cites many routes and names Companions and Successors who transmitted them.
rows.anchor: وهذا الذي وقع تأويل الآية به لا يعارضه حديث الاستنطاق في عالم الذر على تقدير صحته

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: In Ubayy ibn Kaʿb's version, after eliciting their testimony God calls the seven heavens, earth, and Adam as witnesses, warns them not to associate partners, promises messengers and books, and they affirm that He alone is their Lord and God.
rows.anchor: منها في الموطأ ومسند أحمد وإسحاق بن راهويه ومحمد بن نصر المروزي وأبي يعلى الموصلي ومستدرك الحاكم وكتاب المائتين لأبي عثمان الصابوني عن صحابة وتابعين مرفوعا وموقوفا - منهم عمر وأبي بن كعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author concludes that two covenants were taken: an inward, rational one through evidence and an outward, verbal one conveyed by messengers, reflecting special care for humanity and its honored, serious purpose.
rows.anchor: والحاصل أنه أخذ علينا عهدان : أحدهما حالي تهدى إليه العقول , وهو نصب الآدلة والآخر مقالي اخبرت به الرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding stories show most people perish; the verse swears that many jinn and humans are brought toward Hell, a claim hard to believe because humans can be worse than beasts.
rows.anchor: ولقد } وعزتنا وجلالنا { ذرأنا } أي خلقنا بعظمتنا وأنشأنا وبثثنا ونشرنا { لجهنم كثيرا } أي ألجأناهم إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jinn are mentioned first because people exalt and fear them and are misled by them: they are the true objects of worship when they persuade humans to worship other than God; humans worship what is unworthy.
rows.anchor: فهم في الحقيقة المعبودون لا الحجارة , ونحوها { والإنس } أي بعبادتهم لمن لا يصلح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their hearts fail at the understanding required of them: reflecting on proofs of God's oneness, prophethood, and its consequences, the beneficial understanding taught by scripture and messengers.
rows.anchor: وهو النظر في أدلة التوحيد وثبوت النبوة وما تفرغ عن ذلك , وههو الفقه المسعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their eyes see visible signs without reflective consideration, and their ears hear revealed signs without recollection or thought; the problem is failure to use these faculties beneficially.
rows.anchor: الآيات المرئية إبصار تفكر واعتبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They resemble livestock in lacking understanding, yet are worse: animals flee danger and seek water and pasture, while humans can reason from perception but neglect that ability.
rows.anchor: والأنعام لا قدرة لها على ما يترتب على هذه المدارك من الفقه . وهؤلاء مع قدرتهم على ذلك أهملوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans who strive against desire for perfection can rise above angels because of their struggle.
rows.anchor: من طلب الكمال وسعى له سعيه مع نزاع الشهوات علا عن درجة الملائكة بما قاسى من الجهاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only these people are truly heedless: animals may be unaware of what is intended for them, but they are not blind and deaf to useful things or doomed to eternal punishment.
rows.anchor: فقد أشارت الآية إلى تفصيل الإنسان على الملك كما اقتضيته سورة الزيتون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans are intermediate between angels, who are pure intellect, and animals, who are pure desire: reason's victory raises them above angels, while desire's victory lowers them beneath animals; the author links this to 95:5.
rows.anchor: أحسن تقويم } ) 77 [ التين : 5 ] وإن غلبت شهوته كان اسفل من الحيوان بما أضاع من عقله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing people as misguided, the author prevents the inference that God is unworthy: only God possesses every beautiful name and attribute of perfection, free of deficiency and temporal change.
rows.anchor: { الأسماء } ولما كان الاسم إذالحظت فيه الناسبه كان بمعنى الصفة , أنث في قوله { الحسنى } أي كلها باتصافه دون غيره بصفات الكمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author argues from contingency: changing created things are possible and need a chooser to prefer existence; this establishes God's free choice and power, then wisdom, knowledge, life, hearing, sight, speech, will, and unity, since otherwise disorder would follow.
rows.anchor: كل ممكن محتاج وأدنى ما يحتاج إلى مرجح يرجح وجوده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Call on God through His names by describing, naming, and asking Him with them; remembrance frees the heart from worldly desire and affliction, and God's many names display the greatness of their bearer without compromising oneness.
rows.anchor: { فادعوه } أي فصفوه وسموه واسألوه { بها } لتنجوا من جهنم وتنالوا كل ما تحمد عاقبته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who deviate in God's names either assign them to others, thereby implying all divine attributes, or use unauthorized names; some are permissible only alongside their complement, while names implying deficiency are forbidden.
rows.anchor: { في أسمائه } أي فيطلقونها على غيره بأن يسموه إلها , فليزمهم أن يطلقوا عليه جميع أوصاف الإله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Examples of illicit naming include calling God father or body, using a derivative like 'teacher' merely because He is knowing, naming Him with a term suggesting deficient creatures, or invoking an unknown term despite popular praise.
rows.anchor: مثل إطلاق الأب عليه والجسم , وكذا كل ما أهم نقصا , فلم يكن أحسن

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān, transmitting from Ibn al-Sikkīt, says the simple and derived forms of the verb both mean deviating from truth and introducing what does not belong to it.
rows.anchor: العدول عن الحق والإدخال فيه ما ليس منه - نقله أبو حيان عن ابن السكيت

rows.speaker: الإمام أبو القاسم علي بن جعفر بن القطاع
rows.claim: Ibn al-Qaṭṭāʿ's lexicon gives laḥada as making a lateral grave niche and as inclining toward, away from, or within religion; both forms are read accordingly.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو القاسم علي بن جعفر بن القطاع في كتاب الأفعال : لحد الميت لحدا وألحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive 'they will be recompensed' emphasizes that the warning is about the occurrence of retribution, not who inflicts it; it applies in this world and the next, as an unfailing promise.
rows.anchor: وكان المرهب إيقاع الجزاء , لاكونه من معين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their punishment corresponds to their habitual acts; after describing those destined for Hell, the author transitions to the remaining group among God's creation, introduced in 7:181.
rows.anchor: ولما أخبر تعالى عن ذرء جهنم من القبلتين , تشوف السامع إلى معرفة حال الباقين منهما

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawī reports that a group of Jews attended the battle of Badr to see which side would prevail.
rows.anchor: أن جماعة من اليهود حضروا قتال بدر لينظروا على من تكون الدائرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Considering the comparison with Pharaoh's people, the author says the passage mainly targets the Jews; calling them people who do not understand is a severe rebuke, as in 59:13.
rows.anchor: علمت أن جل المقصود من هذه الآيات إلى قوله { ذلك بأنهم قومك لا يفقهون } اليهود , وفي تعبيره ب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment is for what their hands sent, their audacity toward God; God's complete ownership also permits Him to act without a prior offense, and He is not unjust because all belongs to Him and He is not questioned for His acts.
rows.anchor: بما قدمت أيديكم } اي من الجراءة على الله { وأن } أي وبسبب أن له أن يفعل ذلك وإن لم تقدموا شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, 'not unjust to the servants' means God does not let an oppressor wrong the oppressed without requiting the wrong; the author points ahead to the phrasing in Sūrat Fuṣṣilat.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المعنى : وليس بذي ظلم لأنه لا يترك الظالم يبغي على المظلوم من غير جزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dāʾb means the settled habit or conduct of these disbelievers; the pattern recurs across eras and places, like Pharaoh's people and those before them who denied messengers.
rows.anchor: كدأب } أي عادة هؤلاء الكفار وشأنهم الذي دأبوا فيه وداموا وواظبوا فمونوا عليه كعادة { آل فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier peoples were destroyed by wind, blast, drowning, or being swallowed by the earth, not combat; this explains 'you did not kill them' and shows God destroys enemies through battle or otherwise.
rows.anchor: كان هلاكهم بغير قتال , بل بعضهم باليح وبعضهم بالصحية وبعضهم بالغرق وبعضهم بالخسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one should claim personal credit for an act, including killing an enemy God killed or disputing spoils; the author connects this discipline to 57:23 and the Prophet's habit of attributing outcomes to God.
rows.anchor: لا ينسب أحد لنفسه فعلا , فإنه لا فرق عندي في إهلاك أعدائي بين أن يكون إهلاكهم بتسليط من قتال أو غيره

rows.speaker: كعب بن زهير
rows.claim: Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr praises the believers as neither boastful when their spears prevail nor distressed when they themselves are struck.
rows.anchor: ليسوا مفاريح إن نالت رماحهم قوما وليسوا مجازيعا إذا نيلوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelieving in God's signs means covering the evidence that reason's light reveals and preventing followers from acting on it; God then seized them in overpowering punishment for their sins.
rows.anchor: { كفروا بآيات الله } أي ستروا ما دلتهم عليه أنوار عقولهم من دلالات الملك الأعلى وغطوها لأنهم لم يعملوا بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image of God's majesty portrays His awe as overwhelming human powers and bringing down the disbelievers; God is strong, defeats all, and cannot be defeated, and His punishment is severe.
rows.anchor: { إن الله } أي الذي له الإحاطة الشامله { قوي } أي يغلب كل شيء ولا يغلبه شيء { شديد العقاب * }
